s1.syndrome_frame: Congenital skin lesion with atrophic plaque and vascular features
salient_findings: Single, nonpulsatile, well-demarcated, dark brown atrophic plaque
Linear midline depression and elevated, compressible, soft border
Visible small vein within the plaque and extensive network of small superficial branching vessels
key_facts: Congenital skin lesion on the left supraclavicular area
Lesion measured 11 cm × 3.5 cm at birth and 10 cm × 2.5 cm at 5 months
Lesion has a linear midline depression and an elevated, compressible, soft border
Small vein (~0.3 mm) visible to the naked eye within the plaque
Extensive network of small superficial branching vessels localized to the area of the atrophic plaque
Patient is healthy and not on medications
Birth and neonatal history were unremarkable

shortlist.label: Rapidly involuting congenital hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical description of a congenital skin lesion with atrophic plaque and vascular features

shortlist.label: Smooth muscle hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: Considered in initial differential diagnosis for a congenital skin lesion

shortlist.label: Semiannular lipoatrophy
shortlist.why_kept: Initially considered for a congenital skin lesion with atrophic features

shortlist.label: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis for a congenital vascular lesion with atrophic plaque

shortlist.label: Congenital hemangioma, non-involuting
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and vascular features are consistent with this diagnosis

raw.rationale: The lesion's size decreased from birth to 5 months, and the presence of an extensive network of small superficial branching vessels supports this diagnosis

rejected.label: Smooth muscle hamartoma
rejected.why: Lack of characteristic features such as follicular pits or hypertrichosis

rejected.label: Semiannular lipoatrophy
rejected.why: Typically presents with atrophy of subcutaneous fat and does not usually have a network of superficial vessels

rejected.label: Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome
rejected.why: Usually involves multiple systems and has a more complex presentation, including varicose veins and bony or soft tissue hypertrophy

rejected.label: Congenital hemangioma, non-involuting
rejected.why: The lesion's decrease in size from birth to 5 months suggests involution, which is not characteristic of non-involuting congenital hemangiomas
